**Wave 1 is not optional, and it is not this bundle's payment.** `F225` and `F226` are already minted: the archived `C-ROOT-WINDOW` row's `<Pays>` names both, so the payer map (`derivePayerMap` over the real archive and both registry layers, 80 tokens at this commit) claims them the moment they are live. The shipped validator refuses any committed tree holding them without the move (`finding-eligible-still-live`, driven: exactly two findings, both naming archive event `C-ROOT-WINDOW`), so their flush and their `--retire` are one execution wave, and the tree the commit holds is the moved state. The flush is also the last thing the staged buffer's disposition names for them: `F233` records, as the maintainer's decision, that `F226` flushes as-is and retires under the `PaidBy` its already-minted row produces even though the bundle that row names never touched a skill — the authority's error, recorded in the record beside the finding it misattributes, and not reopened here.
**Wave 1 breaks the shipped suite, loudly and on purpose.** The `C-ROOT-WINDOW` payment invariant ships a zero-carriers pin: no `<Finding>` in either findings file may carry `F225` or `F226` — *the pre-payment waits for the next flush*. The flush is the next flush. The driven faithful copy shows `validate:ci` exiting 1 after wave 1's move on exactly that one assertion out of 1809, so the committed tree would be red without the repair, and the repair is therefore part of the same execution wave. The defect class is settled in this record three times: a pin on a finding's liveness (`F225`), a fixture planted into the live layer (`F229`), and now a token asserted absent (`F232`) — a check written against the state that existed at approval rather than the state the record's own rules produce next. The payment-invariant form the staged `F232` states is the PR #86 repair's shape a second time: it keeps what survives payment and pins nothing that the record's designed life cycle will undo.
**Wave 2 fits because the window says so, and two entries stay out for the same reason.** The live findings root reads `base="7711" headroom="135" ceiling="7846"` at this commit. The five wave-2 entries total 129 element lines by the shipped rule (read back on the driven copy: `base="7840" headroom="6" ceiling="7846"`), and the two entries left staged total more than the remaining window can hold with them. No wave-2 body cites `f230` or `f233`, so their staying staged breaks no citation closure, and their staged dispositions name other bundles' work.
**The close pays its own flush's repair.** The row the plan mints makes `F232` eligible only when the bundle is archived, so the mint is invisible to the committed tree and the close's single `--retire` is the payment: moved 2, the finding stamped and landed in the retired sibling, the row beside it, the index layer flipped in place.
